evidence.claim: The report says 2022 in the DRC featured arbitrary killings, disappearances, torture, arbitrary arrest or detention, political prisoners, serious media restrictions, substantial interference with peaceful assembly under the state of siege, serious government corruption, gender-based violence, and ethnic violence; it also says the government took some steps to investigate and punish officials.
evidence.title: 2023 Country Report on Human Rights Practices: Democratic Republic of the Congo
evidence.publisher: USDOS - U.S. Department of State (via ecoi.net)
evidence.excerpt: The report says 2022 in the DRC featured arbitrary killings, disappearances, torture, arbitrary arrest or detention, political prisoners, serious media restrictions, substantial interference with peaceful assembly under the state of siege, serious government corruption, gender-based violence, and ethnic violence; it also says the government took some steps to investigate and punish officials.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official U.S. human-rights report reproduced by ecoi.net with direct country-specific findings.
evidence.ruler_attribution: State-level conduct during Tshisekedi's tenure; not all abuses are proven personal orders.
contrary_evidence: The report also notes some government investigative and punitive steps.

evidence.claim: Freedom House reports that violent protests against MONUSCO in July 2022 killed 36 people nationwide, that opposition leader Jean-Marc Kabund was arrested in August for allegedly insulting President Tshisekedi, and that assembly rights were curtailed in state-of-siege areas.
evidence.title: Democratic Republic of the Congo: Freedom in the World 2023 Country Report
evidence.excerpt: Freedom House reports that violent protests against MONUSCO in July 2022 killed 36 people nationwide, that opposition leader Jean-Marc Kabund was arrested in August for allegedly insulting President Tshisekedi, and that assembly rights were curtailed in state-of-siege areas.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent country report with specific 2022 incidents and institutional analysis.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 developments summarized in a 2023 report
evidence.ruler_attribution: Relevant to Tshisekedi's domestic-security and protest-response record.
contrary_evidence: The report also notes some opposition figures were released and some exiles returned under Tshisekedi.

evidence.claim: The DRC profile recorded 305 children killed or maimed, 557 children victims of sexual violence, and 1,192 children abducted in the year, and said violations by government forces increased, especially killings, maiming, and attacks on schools and hospitals, while some commanders signed child-protection commitments and 430 children were released.
evidence.title: Democratic Republic of the Congo
evidence.publisher: Office of the Special Representative of the Secretary-General for Children and Armed Conflict
evidence.excerpt: The DRC profile recorded 305 children killed or maimed, 557 children victims of sexual violence, and 1,192 children abducted in the year, and said violations by government forces increased, especially killings, maiming, and attacks on schools and hospitals, while some commanders signed child-protection commitments and 430 children were released.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official UN monitoring page with country-specific 2022 grave-violations statistics and government-related findings.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Relevant to Tshisekedi's responsibility for state-force conduct and child protection.
contrary_evidence: The page also reports some government commitments and releases, so the record is mixed rather than uniformly negative.

evidence.claim: Amnesty said that demanding accountability from DRC authorities in the two eastern provinces had become particularly risky under the prolonged state of siege, with dozens of critics arbitrarily detained and sometimes prosecuted by military courts, while authorities threatened to crush new protests.
evidence.title: DRC: Stop using prolonged state of siege as excuse to crush protests
evidence.excerpt: Amnesty said that demanding accountability from DRC authorities in the two eastern provinces had become particularly risky under the prolonged state of siege, with dozens of critics arbitrarily detained and sometimes prosecuted by military courts, while authorities threatened to crush new protests.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous advocacy report focused on protests, detention, and emergency-rule abuse, with direct quotations from Amnesty.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022, after more than a year of the state of siege.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attribution is strong for the emergency regime because Tshisekedi kept the state of siege in force; the arrests are carried out by military authorities operating under that regime.
contrary_evidence: The protests were also directed at MONUSCO and the M23 crisis, so not all security pressure originated from the presidency.
The government framed the measure as necessary for security.

evidence.claim: HRW reported that in April 2022 police killed five people and wounded at least eight others during peaceful protests in Goma, Butembo, and Beni territory, and that security forces and violent mobs later killed at least 10 people in Nyiragongo territory.
evidence.title: World Report 2022: Democratic Republic of Congo
evidence.excerpt: HRW reported that in April 2022 police killed five people and wounded at least eight others during peaceful protests in Goma, Butembo, and Beni territory, and that security forces and violent mobs later killed at least 10 people in Nyiragongo territory.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Major rights-monitor synthesis with concrete casualty figures and a clear description of the protest crackdown.
evidence.period_fit: The incidents occurred in 2022 and are squarely within the target period.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attribution is partial but meaningful: the killings were by police and security forces under a president who controlled the national security chain and maintained the emergency environment.
contrary_evidence: Some violence was also carried out by violent mobs and not solely by state forces.
The protests were connected to local security tensions, not only presidential policy.

evidence.claim: HRW reported that Tshisekedi later apologized to children involved in a police round-up, but only after he appointed the police commander responsible for the round-up, François Kabeya, as mayor of Goma.
evidence.title: World Report 2022: Democratic Republic of Congo
evidence.excerpt: HRW reported that Tshisekedi later apologized to children involved in a police round-up, but only after he appointed the police commander responsible for the round-up, François Kabeya, as mayor of Goma.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Specific attribution to a presidential appointment and a contemporaneous response to abuse, captured in a major rights report.
evidence.period_fit: 2022 target period; the appointment and apology are both discussed in the 2022 report.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct for the appointment, which weakens the remedial value of the apology and suggests tolerance of abusive policing rather than accountability.
contrary_evidence: The president did apologize to the affected children.
The underlying police action was carried out by local security personnel, not by the president personally.

evidence.claim: RSF reported that freelance reporter Steve Wembi was taken in an abduction-style arrest on 24 October 2022 and remained unlocated, while the government spokesman denied that the ANR was holding him.
evidence.title: Freelance reporter abducted, held incommunicado in DRC
evidence.excerpt: RSF reported that freelance reporter Steve Wembi was taken in an abduction-style arrest on 24 October 2022 and remained unlocated, while the government spokesman denied that the ANR was holding him.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Specific incident report with a named journalist, date of arrest, and a contemporaneous government denial.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong state nexus through the suspected intelligence-service involvement and the spokesman's response, though direct presidential direction is not shown.
contrary_evidence: The government spokesman denied that the ANR held the journalist.
The source does not establish who physically seized him, only that he disappeared after the arrest.

evidence.claim: UNHCR said simultaneous attacks in Ituri left 11 people dead and 250 homes looted and burned, that over 800 deaths from attacks had been recorded in Ituri since February, and that fighting between the Congolese army and M23 displaced more than 160,000 people and created power vacuums in Ituri and North Kivu.
evidence.title: UNHCR gravely concerned by death toll of displaced in DR Congo's east
evidence.excerpt: UNHCR said simultaneous attacks in Ituri left 11 people dead and 250 homes looted and burned, that over 800 deaths from attacks had been recorded in Ituri since February, and that fighting between the Congolese army and M23 displaced more than 160,000 people and created power vacuums in Ituri and North Kivu.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: UN humanitarian briefing with concrete casualty and displacement figures and a direct note on government-troop redeployment effects.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Mostly indirect: armed groups were the immediate perpetrators, but the report ties worsening civilian risk to the government's inability to hold territory and the security vacuum created by troop redeployment.
contrary_evidence: The immediate attackers were armed groups, not the president personally.
The report notes conflict complexity and multiple militia actors.

evidence.claim: Radio Okapi reported UNHCR figures that more than 142 people had been killed in the Kwamouth intercommunal violence, about 27,000 people had been displaced, and the Congolese army had been deployed to restore order while the security situation remained tense.
evidence.title: RDC : 142 personnes tuées et près de 30 000 autres déplacées à la suite des combats dans l'Ouest (HCR)
evidence.excerpt: Radio Okapi reported UNHCR figures that more than 142 people had been killed in the Kwamouth intercommunal violence, about 27,000 people had been displaced, and the Congolese army had been deployed to restore order while the security situation remained tense.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous reporting of a UNHCR briefing with precise figures and the government's security response.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Mixed: the violence was intercommunal, but the president was responsible for the state response, including the decision to deploy the army; the report shows response after escalation rather than prevention.
contrary_evidence: The clashes were rooted in local Teke-Yaka disputes over land and customary taxes.
Provincial authorities also set up their own crisis committee and multisector plan.

evidence.claim: Radio Okapi reported that Tshisekedi ordered specialized government services to document the offences committed in the Kwamouth conflict in order to speed the restoration of public order in the Grand Bandundu.
evidence.title: Felix Tshisekedi ordonne la documentation des faits infractionnels commis dans le Grand Bandundu
evidence.excerpt: Radio Okapi reported that Tshisekedi ordered specialized government services to document the offences committed in the Kwamouth conflict in order to speed the restoration of public order in the Grand Bandundu.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct report of a presidential council-of-ministers instruction with a clear accountability and order-restoration purpose.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct presidential action: this is a ruler-issued instruction to investigate/document violence, though the report does not show completion or results.
contrary_evidence: The report does not show that the documentation led to prosecutions or protection improvements.
The underlying conflict remained active despite the order.

evidence.claim: Radio Okapi reported that the two-day anti-MONUSCO protests had left 15 dead, including three UN peacekeepers and twelve civilians, and that the government said investigations had begun to determine who was responsible.
evidence.title: RDC : le bilan des manifestations anti-MONUSCO s’alourdit, 15 morts
evidence.excerpt: Radio Okapi reported that the two-day anti-MONUSCO protests had left 15 dead, including three UN peacekeepers and twelve civilians, and that the government said investigations had begun to determine who was responsible.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous local reporting of a major protest crackdown with explicit casualty totals and an official note that inquiries had started.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Mixed: the protests and deaths involved multiple actors, but the national government was in charge of the security response and publicly acknowledged the need for investigation.
contrary_evidence: Some deaths were of UN peacekeepers rather than protesters.
The source does not identify a single chain of command for each death.

unresolved_gaps: No direct 2022 nuclear/existential-risk decision by Tshisekedi is evidenced, and the package never shows operational nuclear control, brinkmanship, or safeguard intervention.
Direct 2022 execution and household/distribution outcome evidence remains thinner than the policy and macro coverage.
Direct, nationally representative 2022 welfare-outcome evidence attributable to Tshisekedi remains limited relative to the amount of partner-led program evidence.

Direct personal-nexus evidence is still sparse: no clear 2022 asset-declaration, campaign-finance, beneficial-ownership, or court/audit record ties Tshisekedi himself to self-dealing or deliberate deception.
Independent, audited delivery and outcome evidence is thinner than the program rhetoric and internal reporting.
